thread:
sam: FYI bringing up syzygy-11b (int4) canary on dedicated. After ~6h we're seeing p95 latency jump ~2x and memory fragmentation creeping up. No immediate hard OOM but lots of backend retries. rolling back to int8?

elena: Can you paste the logs / bench command you used? Also what's the canary default for max_new_tokens and batch size?

sam: Repro command I used locally: ```./bench --model syzygy-11b --quant int4 --batch 8 --max_new 256 --prefetch 1```

sam: Example tail of worker log: ```2026-03-18T14:12:08Z ERROR allocation failed: cudaMalloc 0x7f... size=128MB
kv_cache_used=1.2GB kv_slots=9 free_slots=2 compactor_runs=3```

matt: That `--max_new 256` is probably the main driver — larger generation window increases KV churn and triggers fragmentation with int4 kernels. For canary we should be conservative: set default max_new_tokens=128 and batch=4.

jules: Also try disabling prefetch (set --prefetch 0) on the int4 variant to avoid extra transient allocations. Prefetch helps under int8 but with the current allocator pattern it's hurting QC for int4.

perf-bot: Canary 6501234567 started 2026-03-18T08:00Z. Baseline (int8) p50=85ms p95=240ms tokens/sec=620. Current (int4 canary) p50=95ms p95=520ms tokens/sec=610.

elena: Good data. Two parallel actions: 1) short-term tweak defaults (max_new_tokens=128, batch=4, prefetch=0), 2) run a targeted bench/soak for 6h with compaction enabled every 5m. I can push a canary patch for that.

sam: I'll queue the patch. Also observed small quality regression on our summarization eval with int4 (~0.6% Rouge drop). Not huge but above our rollback threshold of 0.5%.

jules: For quality, we should gate on eval set: if quality delta >0.5% revert to int8 for that model. We can still keep int4 for cheaper, but route production traffic to int8 for high-quality routes.

matt: Longer-term: look into kernel-level fused allocations and better slot compaction heuristics. The allocator is leaving small free segments that build up. Turn on aggressive compaction in the runtime (compaction_interval=300s, eviction_threshold=0.6) for the canary and monitor fragmentation metrics.

ops-bot: Scheduled rollback check: will auto-rollback canary if p95 > 400ms for 10 continuous minutes.

elena: I'll run the bench harness with the smaller defaults and the compactor on the int4 canary and post the numbers here in ~2h. Also will run the per-prompt eval harness to confirm the 0.6% delta isn't concentrated on a small subset. :eyes:

sam: thanks — immediate plan: push defaults patch (max_new_tokens=128, batch=4, prefetch=0), enable compaction sweep 5m, start 6h soak. If soak looks stable and quality delta <0.5% we can try gradual traffic ramp. If not, revert to int8 and open follow-up issue for kernel/alloc fixes.

elena: ack. posting reproduce script and perf collection commands to the thread after runs.

sam: (after 2h) quick update: preliminary numbers look better — p95 down to ~300ms with compaction and reduced defaults. continuing soak.

perf-bot: Canary 6501234567 metrics updated: p50=92ms p95=305ms tokens/sec=605 fragmentation_score=0.18

jules: Nice. Keep the soak going. We'll follow up with a short RFC for default max_new_tokens per family (small/med/large) once soak completes.
